surfaces.part: top cap (white plate with teal underside)
sign panel with exit number on shaft

answer.evidence: The cap spans rows 1-7. Its width profile is 7, 11, 11, 13, 13, 13, 13, then 7 for the shaft. It is rounded only at the upper edge and ends flat at width 13 directly on the narrower shaft, so it is a hat/dome and not an ellipse plate. Even so, rows 2-5 are a light (L~235) top band. Rows 6-7 are a darker teal band (L=91) that works as the front-edge line and eave shadow, so the cap shows 4 top rows. Below it the shaft (rows 8-26, width 7) carries the sign panel, and rows 27-30 are a wider base (width 11). The front face is well over 3 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a bollard-style exit-number sign with a rounded cap, a pale shaft and a yellow panel with a '4'. It is small and thin. Measured facts are on par with the references: 12 visible tones per tile matches kiosk-a (12), is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted rather than black. It reads as a dark blue-grey tone beside the material, like the references, and not as a uniform sticker line. The cap and shaft have about 4 lightness steps, with a highlight on the left and shadow on the right, against about 5 on the references. Texture is modest, with a few grain dots on the shaft. Overall it is cleanly drawn and sits acceptably next to the shipped modern_city props, only slightly less rich than the vending machine.
